en.name: Crumpets
en.summary: Crumpets keep 2–3 days in their bag at room temperature, 1–2 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 3 months at −18 °C (0 °F). This is the one bread product where the fridge is genuinely the right answer, because you toast a crumpet anyway and toasting undoes the staling.
en.pantry: 2–3 days in their bag at room temperature, or to the printed date on a supermarket pack. Crumpets are wetter than any bread on this site — they are a pourable yeast-and-soda batter, cooked on one side only, with an open humid crumb and those famous holes running right through it. That makes them a fast mould substrate, and a bag of crumpets in a warm kitchen will show blue-green spots within a few days. The 2–3 day figure is our own judgement rather than a published number.
en.fridge: 1–2 weeks at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, in their bag, and it is worth understanding why this contradicts the usual advice about bread. Refrigeration's penalty is accelerated staling — starch retrogradation is fastest just above freezing — but you are going to toast a crumpet anyway, and toasting reverses staling by re-gelatinising the starch. So you pay nothing, and you buy real time against mould: the bread study cited here found no visible mould at all over ten days at fridge temperature. The published line for shop-bought bread and baked goods is longer still; we have trimmed it because crumpets hold far more water than a pan loaf.
en.freezer: 3 months at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality, a figure read across from commercially baked sliced bread. Freeze them interleaved so they peel apart, in a bag with the air pressed out, and toast them from frozen on a slightly longer setting — no thawing needed and no quality loss worth mentioning. Kept continuously frozen they stay safe beyond that window; what the timeline describes is drying, ice crystals and freezer burn.
en.thawing: Toast straight from frozen. If you thaw them, do it in the fridge — a crumpet left out on a warm counter is a wet, low-acid starch and should not sit around.
spoilage: Blue-green or white fuzzy spots, often down inside the holes where you cannot see them.
A sour, yeasty or alcoholic smell when the bag is opened.
A dense, rubbery texture that stays rubbery after toasting.
tips: Look inside the holes, not just at the surface — mould starts where it is damp and dark.
The fridge is the right place for these, unlike almost every other bread.
Freeze them interleaved so you can take one at a time.
Toast from frozen on a longer setting rather than thawing first.

faq.a: 2–3 days at room temperature, 1–2 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 3 months frozen at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Should crumpets be kept in the fridge?
faq.a: Yes — this is the exception to the rule about bread. The fridge stales them, but you toast them anyway, and toasting undoes staling while buying you real time against mould.
Yes, 3 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Freeze them interleaved and toast straight from frozen on a longer setting.

zh.name: 英式煎餅
zh.summary: 英式煎餅裝在原袋放室溫可放 2～3 天，4 °C 以下冷藏 1～2 週，−18 °C 冷凍 3 個月。這是全站唯一一種「冷藏才是正解」的麵包製品，因為你反正要把它烤過，而烤過正好把老化抵消掉。
zh.pantry: 裝在原袋放室溫 2～3 天，或依超市包裝上的印製日期。它比本站任何一種麵包都濕——那是可以用倒的酵母加小蘇打麵糊、只煎單面，內裡開放又潮濕，招牌的那些孔還一路通到底。這讓它成為長霉的絕佳溫床，一袋放在溫暖廚房裡的煎餅，幾天內就會出現藍綠色霉點。2～3 天這個數字是我們自己的判斷，不是公布的數據。
zh.fridge: 裝在原袋、放 4 °C 以下 1～2 週，而且值得搞懂它為什麼跟一般的麵包建議相反。冷藏的代價是加速老化——澱粉回凝在略高於冰點時最快——但你反正要把煎餅烤過，而烤會讓澱粉重新糊化，把老化逆轉回來。所以你什麼代價都沒付，卻買到了對抗霉的真實時間：這裡引用的麵包研究發現，在冷藏溫度下放十天，完全沒有出現肉眼可見的霉。市售麵包與烘焙品的公布數字還更長一些，我們把它往下修了，因為煎餅的含水量遠高於吐司。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 3 個月品質最好，這個數字是比照市售切片麵包而來。每片之間夾紙冷凍才撕得開，裝袋前壓掉空氣，要吃時直接從冷凍烤、時間調長一點——不必解凍，品質損失也小到不值一提。只要全程沒退冰，超過這個期限仍然安全；期限描述的是變乾、冰晶和凍燒。
zh.thawing: 直接從冷凍烤。真要解凍就放冷藏——一片煎餅是又濕又低酸的澱粉，不該擱在溫暖的檯面上。
spoilage: 出現藍綠色或白色絨毛霉，常常藏在你看不到的孔洞深處。
打開袋子聞到發酸、酵母味或酒精味。
質地變得又密又像橡皮，烤過還是橡皮。
tips: 不要只看表面，往孔洞裡看——霉都是從又濕又暗的地方開始。
和幾乎所有麵包相反，冷藏對它才是對的。
每片之間夾紙冷凍，才能一次只拿一片。
直接從冷凍烤、時間調長，不要先解凍。

faq.a: 室溫 2～3 天，4 °C 以下冷藏 1～2 週，或 −18 °C 冷凍 3 個月。
要——這是麵包規則裡的例外。冷藏會讓它老化，但你反正要烤，而烤能把老化逆轉回來，同時替你擋掉霉。
可以，−18 °C 下 3 個月。夾紙冷凍，要吃時直接從冷凍烤、時間調長一點。
